title: Effects of self-regulated vocabulary learning with chatbots on incidental and collocational vocabulary learning and foreign language learning boredom
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether integrating generative AI chatbots into self-regulated vocabulary learning improves English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners’ incidental vocabulary learning, receptive knowledge of collocations, and foreign language learning boredom. The study addresses a gap in prior research by focusing not only on vocabulary gains but also on collocation learning and affective outcomes such as boredom, while also exploring learners’ attitudes toward chatbot-assisted learning.

The intervention used ChatGPT as a chatbot within a self-regulated learning framework. Across 18 instructional sessions, the experimental group used chatbot-supported strategies including self-monitoring, mnemonic techniques, personalized feedback, contextualized examples, and dialogic interaction. The control group studied the same reading texts, vocabulary targets, and self-regulated learning strategies, but through traditional teacher-led instruction without AI tools. Quantitative data came from pre/post vocabulary tests, collocation tests, and a modified foreign language learning boredom scale, while qualitative data came from semi-structured interviews with 16 experimental-group students.

Participants were 187 B2-level EFL learners aged 17 to 22 from three English language institutes in Türkiye. Ninety-four learners were assigned to the experimental group and ninety-three to the control group. The context was institute-based language instruction with relatively limited routine technology integration, making chatbot use a novel intervention in this setting.

The study found that the chatbot-supported group significantly outperformed the control group on incidental vocabulary and receptive collocation posttests and reported significantly lower boredom. Interview findings reinforced these results, with students describing greater motivation, autonomy, enjoyment, confidence, and reduced anxiety. The authors conclude that generative AI chatbots can create personalized and engaging EFL learning environments that support self-regulated vocabulary learning and improve both linguistic and affective outcomes, though generalizability is limited by convenience sampling and the absence of delayed follow-up testing.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: A named generative AI chatbot by OpenAI that provides conversational interaction, real-time responses, and personalized feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the chatbot in 18 self-regulated vocabulary learning sessions for EFL learners to support incidental vocabulary learning, receptive collocation learning, and reduce foreign language learning boredom.

findings.finding_summary: In a quasi-experimental study with 187 EFL learners (EG n=94; CG n=93), the ChatGPT group scored higher on the vocabulary posttest (M=29.80, SD=6.32) than the control group (M=22.75, SD=7.81). ANCOVA showed a significant group effect on vocabulary posttest scores, F=52.34, p=.00, with Partial Eta Squared=.22, indicating the treatment accounted for 22% of the variance.

For receptive collocation knowledge, the ChatGPT group outperformed the control group on the posttest (EG M=27.92, SD=8.14; CG M=23.24, SD=7.77) in the same quasi-experimental sample of 187 EFL learners. ANCOVA found a significant group effect, F=13.44, p=.00, with Partial Eta Squared=.06, showing the chatbot intervention explained 6% of the variance in collocation outcomes.

The ChatGPT group reported lower foreign language learning boredom at posttest (M=62.36, SD=10.39) than the control group (M=69.81, SD=9.91) among 187 EFL learners. ANCOVA showed a significant group effect on boredom, F=32.31, p=.00, with Partial Eta Squared=.14, suggesting the intervention accounted for 14% of the variance in boredom scores.
findings.measure: Adapted 21-item Foreign Language Learning Boredom Scale (FLLBS)

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical quasi-experimental study with pretest-posttest comparison, random assignment to groups, and ANCOVA analysis, but it is not a full RCT and uses convenience sampling, so some credibility concerns remain.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects include a large vocabulary effect (Partial Eta Squared=.22) and meaningful effects on boredom (.14) and collocation learning (.06), indicating at least one medium-to-large impact outcome.
